page: Microsoft Azure M128-64ms is an x86_64 memory-optimized server instance powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280L processor running at 2.7 GHz. The server is equipped with 3892.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 60.81 GB per core. It also includes 4194 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff between memory capabilities and compute speed. The instance achieves strong uncached memory bandwidth for both large-block read and write operations, placing it in the top 25% of tested servers. However, single-core CPU performance is poor, falling into the bottom 10% across stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests. Multi-core CPU performance, Passmark database operations, and Redis SET operations consistently register in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance is designed for memory-intensive workloads where massive RAM capacity and high uncached memory bandwidth justify the hardware class premium. It is not cost-effective for single-threaded or compute-bound tasks due to its low single-core performance. Appropriate workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise database management systems, and memory-heavy data processing pipelines.
